title: Synthesising Common Ground and Closing a Mediation Round

sections.content: You know *en resumen*, *lo más importante es que* and *destaca que* from B1 Unit 13, *por una parte* and *por otra parte* from B1 Unit 14, and *en definitiva* from B2 Unit 28. When closing a formal mediation round or reading an arbitration ruling (*un laudo*), a mediator combines these markers with higher-register synthesis frames such as *en síntesis*, *cabe destacar que* ('it is worth highlighting that') and *a modo de conclusión*. Together they separate reciprocal concessions from the decisive breakthrough and deliver a binding closing summary for the minutes.

sections.title: Synthesis and Closing Markers in Mediation
rows: Balances reciprocal concessions from the two delegations.
Singles out the key safeguard or turning point in the settlement.
Condenses the agreed points into a single verifiable proposition.
Delivers the overarching assessment or final binding takeaway.

items.spanish: Por una parte, la empresa amplía los turnos; por otra parte, la plantilla acepta el pacto.
items.english: On the one hand, the company expands the shifts; on the other hand, the staff accepts the pact.

items.spanish: Cabe destacar que el arbitraje permitió dirimir la controversia técnica.
items.english: It is worth highlighting that arbitration made it possible to settle the technical controversy.

items.spanish: En síntesis, la avenencia alcanzada evita la vía judicial.
items.english: In synthesis, the agreement reached avoids court proceedings.

items.spanish: En definitiva, un tono conciliador facilitó que se acatara el laudo.
items.english: Ultimately, a conciliatory tone made it easier for the arbitration award to be respected.

sections.content: Keep *por una parte* and *por otra parte* parallel in feminine gender with *parte*: never mix *por una parte* with *por otro*. After *cabe destacar que*, use the indicative because you are presenting an established fact from the session, not a wish.
